modalLead: Config is easier to find your way around. Searching for a setting now finds it wherever it lives, the Overview tells you how much of your setup is no longer standard, and a handful of settings that quietly did nothing have been put right.

items.text: Search now finds every setting, not only the ones you had already looked at. Pressing Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + K and typing webhook found nothing at all unless you happened to have opened that tab first. Every setting is searchable from the moment you open Config.
Settings answer to more than their exact label. Searching uptime, wallpaper, telemetry or hotkey now finds the right setting even when those words appear nowhere on screen.

The Overview says how many settings differ from the standard. The answer to “why does my dashboard behave differently from the guide” used to mean opening every tab and looking for a ↺. The line names the areas involved and takes you straight to them; on an untouched setup it stays out of the way.
Only changed above each tab of settings hides everything still on its standard value, and says how many differ before you press it.
Reset panel puts a whole group back to standard at once, instead of one ↺ at a time. It appears only when something in that group has been changed, and asks first.

sections.title: Settings that did not do what they said

items.text: Background re-check interval now takes effect. Under Behavior › Status & health you could pick how often nextDash re-tests your links in the background, it confirmed Saved, and nothing changed — the checks carried on at their old pace. It now matches the same setting under Data & backups.

Six settings offered to reset themselves on a brand-new install. The ↺ appeared beside settings nobody had touched, and pressing it moved them away from the standard rather than back to it. Among them Retries before offline, Delay between retries and Refresh favicons.

Retries before offline and Delay between retries accepted numbers that were then thrown away. Typing a delay of 5000 reported Saved and left you with 450. The boxes now only offer what actually works.
Clicking “Follow system dark mode” now works. The words beside the tick box did nothing — you had to hit the small box itself, unlike every other tick box in Config.

Toolbar & tabs is split into three groups — the header, and the two halves of the button bar — so the group a setting sits in tells you where on screen to look for it. It was one run of thirteen near-identical tick boxes.
Show all and Hide all for each of those groups, with a count of what is currently showing.

Settings line up. Dropdowns and boxes started at a different place on every row depending on how long its label happened to be, and the ℹ and ↺ buttons sat marooned at the far edge of the panel instead of beside the setting they belong to.

The list of Config sections is one line you can swipe. It used to wrap onto three or four rows above every page, which on a phone was most of the screen before the first setting. Whichever section you open is scrolled into view.
